chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him about al-muzara'ah (sharecropping). I said: A man sows a hundred jarib of land or less or more with food or other things, then a man comes to him and says: Take from me half the price of this seed that you have sown in the land, and half your expenses upon me, and share with me in it. He said: 'There is no harm.' I said: But if what he sows in it he did not buy for a price, and it is merely something he had, he said: 'Then he should value it as it is sold on that day, then he should take half the price and half the expenses and share with him.'

key_terms.النَّفَقَة: Expenses; costs incurred during the cultivation process such as labor or maintenance.
key_terms.الْبَذْر: Seed; the agricultural input provided for sowing.
key_terms.الْمُزَارَعَة: Sharecropping; an agricultural partnership where one party provides land/labor and the other provides capital/seed.
key_terms.جَرِيب: A unit of land area measurement used in classical Islamic jurisprudence.
key_terms.يُقَوِّمْهُ: He should value/assess it; determining the monetary worth of an item based on market conditions.

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for valid sharecropping (muzara'ah) when one party provides capital and the other provides labor and land?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of *muzara'ah* (sharecropping) by addressing the valuation of capital contributions, specifically distinguishing between purchased and pre-owned seed. It establishes that if the seed is already owned, its market value must be assessed to fairly split the cost and expenses with the investor, ensuring equitable profit-sharing. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on precise financial valuation (*taqyeem*) to prevent ambiguity (*gharar*) in agricultural contracts.
